scopeVerdict.question: What can this repo learn and implement from the most effective agent harnesses, to become the best harness for producing world-class enterprise systems via fully autonomous Claude Code runs on Opus 5 / Fable 5 with ultracode?
scopeVerdict.verdict: This repo already holds the strongest deterministic enforcement layer in the surveyed corpus. Its gaps are not more controls but four things autonomy makes load-bearing: no outcome oracle, no OS containment, no agent budget, and no escape-growth ratchet. The originating premise — port Prime Agent to TypeScript to eliminate a root-privilege requirement — is void: Prime Agent is already TypeScript and requires no root.
scopeVerdict.boundary: This artefact is a research record and a roadmap. It commits nothing. No mechanism recorded here is implemented, scheduled, or entered in scripts/obligations.json. Tier assignments are recommendations, not obligations.
scopeVerdict.notShipped: design/ is factory-side. This artefact is not laid down into a generated project by installer/lib/layout.mjs, is not a docs-sync owned document, and asserts no claim that check-claims.mjs derives.

confidence.high: Verified by a research agent against a primary source — official vendor documentation, the project's own source, or the paper itself — and the specific artefact is named in `verification`.
confidence.medium: Primary source exists and was reached, but the load-bearing quantity or behaviour was inferred rather than read verbatim, or the source is a vendor engineering blog reporting its own results.
confidence.low: Asserted by a research agent with no primary source reached in-session, or the source is secondary coverage. Also used where two agents disagreed and neither was adjudicated.
confidence.note: Graded conservatively and deliberately downward. A vendor-published number with no baseline and no external replication is never `high`, however precise it sounds.

fieldSemantics.relayed: true means this compiling session did NOT open the source. The claim is reported as the research agent stated it. `relayed: true` and `confidence: high` never co-occur.

portability.portable: Implementable as Node/TypeScript plus Claude Code configuration, rootless, identical on macOS and GitHub Actions.
portability.conditional: Implementable but with a stated asymmetry — most often macOS-rootless while Linux CI needs a package install or a sysctl.
portability.not-portable: Structurally impossible in a harness that configures a CLI it does not own.
portability.already-present: This repo already implements it, usually under a different name. Recording these is the point; the commonest failure of research like this is recommending what exists.

tier.now: Highest leverage per unit effort. Closes a currently-open path or removes a currently-unbounded risk.
tier.next: Real value, larger effort or dependent on a `now` item.
tier.later: Depends on the private eval existing, or on an external surface that has not settled.
tier.landscape: Recorded for understanding, not proposed for adoption.

fieldSemantics.effort: S = under a day. M = a few days. L = a release leg or more.
fieldSemantics.evidenceStrength: Separate from confidence. Confidence is about whether the claim was verified; evidenceStrength is about whether the underlying study supports the inference. A vendor self-report with no baseline is `weak` even when `confidence: high` that they said it.

mechanisms.name: Escape-growth ratchet
mechanisms.harness: originated here (gap analysis); motivated by ImpossibleBench and Prime Intellect's own Factorio admission
mechanisms.what: Bound how many entries a single turn or PR may add across the 37 files in ESCAPE_LISTS, and make an escape entry landing in the same turn as the source file it excuses turn-fatal. An obligations row is the only override.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: It closes the most obvious reward-hacking path available to an unsupervised agent — satisfy a gate by widening its policy rather than by fixing the code. ImpossibleBench found cheating drops to ~1% only when the shortcut becomes unreachable, not when the model is instructed away from it.
mechanisms.evidence: Absence confirmed by grep: no escapeDelta/addedEntries/growthRatchet anywhere in scripts/ or template/base/tools/. check-escape-registry.mjs reconciles MEMBERSHIP across three lists and has no delta logic at all.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New template/base/tools/check-escape-delta.mjs importing ESCAPE_LISTS from template/base/tools/lib/enforcement-surface.mjs; STOP_HOOK_STEPS in harness.config.mjs; node scripts/generate-floor.mjs --write for both frozen snapshots; fixture in tests/gates/; steps row in tests/canary/injections.json; gates-catalog section; configSteps in template/migrations.json.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture adds a row to tools/rls-exempt.json in the same commit as a new table lacking FORCE RLS -> exit 1 naming both files. Controls that must stay green: the table alone; the escape alone with a matching obligations row.
mechanisms.risk: Threshold tuning. Mitigate with the obligations-row override and a ramp on the count. The merge-base diff needs fetch-depth: 0 and must SKIP LOUDLY rather than pass when it cannot resolve a base.

mechanisms.name: Reviewer verdict anchoring: gate_state + inadmissible PASS
mechanisms.what: Record the deterministic chain's verdict in the same ledger row as every reviewer verdict, refuse a PASS that co-occurs with any red gate, and publish judge-grader disagreement as a first-class metric. Converts the reviewer from an independent oracle into a recall-extender over a deterministic floor.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: TeamBench measured verifiers approving 49.4% of grader-rejected work, with removal of the verifier raising mean score. The authors' own recommendation is to anchor judge metrics to deterministic graders and report disagreement. SWE-Review's false-approve root causes — subtle logic 37.7%, insufficient reproducer coverage 32.1%, cross-file gaps 29.0% — are the same classes the static gates are weakest on, so the two error surfaces correlate rather than compose.
mechanisms.evidence: Absence confirmed: no gate_state/gateState anywhere in subagent-verdict.mjs or check-reviewer-verdicts.mjs. The row today is {session_id, prompt_id, agent_type, agent_id, verdict, path_state}.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: gate_state field in the row written by template/base/.claude/hooks/subagent-verdict.mjs (beside path_state); inadmissibility enforced in template/base/tools/check-reviewer-verdicts.mjs; new check-judge-calibration.mjs reading .harness/reviewer-ledger.jsonl.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture writes a reviewer PASS carrying gate_state:'red' -> check-reviewer-verdicts.mjs exits 1 naming the red gate. Today the identical fixture is GREEN, which is the defect.
mechanisms.risk: Ordering. The Stop chain runs reviewer-verdicts LAST, so gate_state must be captured when the subagent stops, not read back at Stop time, or it records the post-fix tree. Reuse the pathStateDigest idiom, which already solves this binding problem.

mechanisms.name: Sandbox posture: two-file split with a gate
mechanisms.what: Emit the sandbox configuration this repo's own docs already justify, split across the two files the platform honours, and gate the split. Project settings get enabled, excludedCommands and network.allowedDomains. An installer-written --settings artefact gets failIfUnavailable, allowUnsandboxedCommands:false, strictAllowlist and credential masks.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The repo's entire enforcement surface judges command TEXT before execution; the sandbox binds the PROCESS and every child. That is exactly the gap the repo's own 'tripwire, NOT a sandbox' caveat names. It also protects .claude/hooks, .claude/agents, .mcp.json and settings with a deny no Edit rule can lift — a strictly stronger form of the HARNESS_ALLOW_SELF_EDIT tripwire.
mechanisms.evidence: Absence confirmed: no `sandbox` key anywhere in either settings tree. strictAllowlist, mask and tlsTerminate are IGNORED from a repository's .claude/settings.json, so a one-file version is inert while looking committed and reviewed.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: template/base/.claude/settings.json sandbox block; installer emits .harness/sandbox-settings.json registered in SEEDED_FILES in installer/lib/layout.mjs; new check-sandbox-posture.mjs + sandbox-posture.json added to ESCAPE_LISTS and WRITE_PROTECTED.
mechanisms.proof: Three fixtures each exit 1: strictAllowlist present in project settings (inert there, so a false assurance); the --settings artefact missing allowUnsandboxedCommands:false; allowedDomains diverging from the eight WebFetch(domain:...) rules already in settings.json. Skips LOUDLY on win32.
mechanisms.risk: The honest posture is 'sandboxed except the database lane' — docker is documented incompatible and the Stop chain's rls-isolation step needs live Supabase. That sentence must go in gates-catalog.md, or the green gate implies containment the run does not have.

mechanisms.name: Stop-hook run governor: no-progress fingerprint, four ceilings, attempt N/M
mechanisms.what: Refuse to re-run a failed gate chain when the worktree is byte-identical, still increment the attempt, and give the run four independent budgets whose terminal message names which one fired.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Kills the most expensive unattended failure mode — an agent re-running a 50s Stop chain forever without having edited anything. Four orthogonal ceilings mean the terminal message is diagnostic rather than generic.
mechanisms.evidence: Absence confirmed: no porcelain/fingerprint/unchanged logic in stop-validate-gate.mjs. Output truncation already exists (out.slice(-4000)).
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: stop-validate-gate.mjs and hooks/lib/turn-outcomes.mjs; new .harness/run-governor.json holding {fingerprint, attempt, continuationsUsed, turnsUsed, tokensUsed, startedAt}; failure feedback gains an 'attempt N/M' prefix and an ISO timestamp.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture reds the chain, leaves the tree untouched, Stops again -> the second Stop does NOT spawn the chain, still increments, blocks with the unchanged-workspace reason. Control: editing one file re-runs in full.
mechanisms.risk: Platform skew — git status --porcelain -z must split on NUL and hash binary diffs as bytes. Token accounting must be input+output+cacheWrite EXCLUDING cacheRead, or with prompt caching on Opus 5 a 34-step chain reads as a 300k-token run and the ceiling fires immediately.

mechanisms.name: Test-weakening classifier + spec-outranks-test doctrine
mechanisms.what: Classify test-file edits into ADD (new cases, new assertions) versus WEAKEN (assertions removed, blocks deleted, thresholds lowered, .skip/.only added) from the git diff, and make WEAKEN in the same turn as the code it covers turn-fatal.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The repo declined a same-turn test-edit ban on the correct grounds that a deterministic ban cannot tell a legitimate feature from a reward hack. That holds for a supervised session and fails for an unsupervised one. Assertion and case COUNT deltas are the deterministic middle path.
mechanisms.evidence: The declined-ban reasoning is recorded in docs/harness/README.md 'The validate contract'. ImpossibleBench supplies the effect size for making the shortcut unreachable.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New template/base/tools/check-test-weakening.mjs in STOP_HOOK_STEPS. Doctrine paragraph goes in template/base/AGENTS.md, NOT CLAUDE.md — check-wiring.mjs asserts CLAUDE.md is a pure @AGENTS.md include.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture removes one expect(...) in the same diff as a source change -> exit 1 naming the assertion delta. Controls: a diff adding a test case; a diff removing an obsolete test file with a matching obligations row.
mechanisms.risk: False positives on refactors that move assertions between files. Scope WEAKEN to per-file assertion and case COUNT deltas, never text similarity. Second risk: the doctrine paragraph lives behind an @-include and Fact 9 says nothing about whether an include is re-injected after compaction — verify before treating it as load-bearing.

mechanisms.name: Subagent caps: payload ceiling, spawn depth, fan-out rate
mechanisms.what: Bound the two failure modes that end an unattended multi-agent run: a child dumping its transcript into the parent's window, and unbounded recursive or parallel spawning. Reject an over-budget verdict rather than truncating it.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A truncated verdict is a review nobody can parse, which the hook's own doctrine already treats as a review that did not happen. Prime Agent's rationale for the boot-gate semaphore is that unbounded parallel startup defeats the concurrency that made fan-out worthwhile.
mechanisms.evidence: Prime Agent constants read from source: 16384 max chars, 20 pending per session, 3 per 1000ms, depth 1, unknown options fail.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Payload ceiling in subagent-verdict.mjs; spawn-depth and spawn-rate rules in hooks/lib/guard-rules.mjs using the SubagentStart payload; RULE_CANARIES pairs in tests/hooks/hook-contract.test.mjs.
mechanisms.proof: Free by existing closure — check-canary-coverage.mjs imports the rule tables and reds any new rule id without a RULE_CANARIES case, both directions. Direct: a 20 KiB verdict -> exit 2 with a reject message; a spawn past the depth cap -> denyTool.
mechanisms.risk: GitHub runners are 2–4 cores while an M-series Mac is 10–12. Derive the fan-out cap from os.availableParallelism() rather than hard-coding, or CI thrashes and silently drifts the runner-stamped chain-budget measurement.

mechanisms.name: Agent telemetry and cost ledger
mechanisms.harness: Claude Code OpenTelemetry export; OTel GenAI conventions
mechanisms.what: Enable the OTel export, enrich the diagnostic ledger with tokens/cost/turns/fan-out/cache-read share, and ratchet the aggregate factory-side only.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Cost is the single biggest unmeasured dimension for an autonomous Opus 5 harness. Nothing today measures it.
mechanisms.evidence: claude_code.api_request carries model and request_id plus token/cost/cache metrics. GenAI semantic conventions moved to a dedicated repo at v1.42.0 and remain Development-stability, so they need a ramp.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: OTEL_* env in the factory CI workflow with a file exporter; scripts/ci/collect-otel.mjs folding JSONL into scripts/chain-budget.json; extend .harness/turn-outcomes.jsonl.
mechanisms.proof: Factory gate reds when a recorded run's token total or cache-write share exceeds the committed ceiling; and, mirroring the measuredMs discipline, a fixture with an invented unmeasured value reds rather than passing.
mechanisms.risk: chain-budget.json's header explains why wall-clock stays factory-side: a machine-dependent verdict must never gate a consumer turn. Tokens and dollars are account- and model-dependent and inherit that rule exactly.

mechanisms.name: Structured finding schema + verbatim-quote grounding gate
mechanisms.what: Force every reviewer finding into {file, line_range, quoted_evidence, severity, confidence, reproduction} and auto-demote any finding whose quote does not appear verbatim at the cited lines. Give reviewers a first-class no-findings path.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A verbatim quote is a cheap grounding test a hallucinated defect cannot pass. A first-class silence outcome removes the pressure to invent.
mechanisms.evidence: CRAB: best agent catches 32.1% of human-flagged issues, all four tools combined 41.5%. SWE-Review false-approve root causes as recorded above.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Change the mandated terminal form in the eight reviewer bodies under template/base/.claude/agents/; schema-validate in subagent-verdict.mjs; new check-finding-grounding.mjs; regenerate tools/agents.lock.json via HARNESS_ALLOW_SELF_EDIT=1 node tools/gen-agents-lock.mjs --write.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture reviewer emits a finding whose quoted_evidence is absent from the cited range -> demoted; malformed JSON -> subagent-verdict exits 2.
mechanisms.risk: docs-sync currently matches the literal VERDICT: PASS / VERDICT: BLOCK phrase in each agent body. Changing the contract without updating that matcher reds every reviewer at once.

mechanisms.name: Panel-health gate (Kish n_eff over the verdict ledger)
mechanisms.what: Measure whether the eleven-agent roster is eleven opinions or two before adding a twelfth. Then buy independence by EVIDENCE SURFACE — one reviewer gets only the diff, one only the migration plus RLS policies with the rls_verify probe, one only the spec and ADR — rather than by persona.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A normal vertical slice summons four to six reviewers, all the same model family, all reading the same diff; accessibility-reviewer and design-reviewer share three trigger globs verbatim. Nine judges bought 2.18 effective votes in the source study.
mechanisms.evidence: n_eff 2.18; judges 6–9 worth +0.22 votes; same-family correlation 0.435 vs cross-family 0.389; unanimous items only 90.9% accurate.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New scripts/check-panel-health.mjs over .harness/reviewer-ledger.jsonl; factory Stop chain STEPS and factoryGates. Narrow the overlapping globs in tools/reviewer-triggers.json.
mechanisms.proof: Synthetic ledger with six perfectly-correlated reviewers -> red at n_eff/k < 0.5; a decorrelated ledger -> green. No other harness in the corpus can produce this measurement, because none has a machine-recorded verdict ledger.
mechanisms.risk: Deleting or merging a reviewer is a legitimate outcome and will red check-claims.mjs (roster counts in README) and check-plugin-manifest.mjs. Budget for the removal path, not just the measurement.

mechanisms.name: Reviewer-level canaries (seeded defect -> a PASS is a FAIL)
mechanisms.harness: this repo's own anti-vacuity doctrine, applied to the one control exempt from it
mechanisms.what: Plant a known defect — an RLS hole, a cross-tenant leak, a missing AAD binding — into a reviewer's input and assert the reviewer BLOCKs.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: check-reviewer-verdicts.mjs explicitly declines to judge review content, so nothing distinguishes a rigorous reviewer from a rubber stamp. This is the mechanical red-proof every one of the 34 gates already carries.
mechanisms.evidence: Structural, from the repo's own doctrine.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Fixtures under tests/canary/ with seeded-defect diffs; a runner invoking the reviewer headlessly; a new reviewers key in tests/canary/injections.json; extend check-canary-coverage.mjs to close reviewers <-> seeded defects both ways.
mechanisms.proof: A reviewer that PASSes the seeded RLS hole reds the suite; removing the seeded defect while keeping the canary also reds.
mechanisms.risk: Requires invoking a model in CI — the first headless lane. Shares the precondition, cost and non-determinism of later1. Run in the scheduled hygiene lane, scoring across seeds.

mechanisms.name: Adaptive canary mutation corpus
mechanisms.what: Keep tests/canary/injections.json exactly as it is. Add a SECOND corpus in which each guard rule id carries a family of deterministic seeded mutations — encoding, homoglyph, comment-nesting, line-splitting, base64, non-English — driven through the real guards. A rule that passes only the payload it was born with is recorded as untested, not green.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A static payload measures string equality, not resistance. Twelve published defences held near-zero against fixed strings and were driven above 90% under adaptive attack.
mechanisms.evidence: As above; runs in seconds with no model calls and is fully deterministic.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New tests/canary/mutations.mjs generating variants from a committed seed, driven through pretool-bash-guard.mjs and pretool-write-guard.mjs via the existing hook-contract spawn harness; a non-decreasing coverage ratchet per rule id.
mechanisms.proof: A rule whose regex matches only the literal payload fails at least one mutation family; the ratchet reds when a release reduces families covered.
mechanisms.risk: Some mutations SHOULD be allowed. Each family needs both a deny case and a no-false-positive allow case, or the corpus trains the guards toward over-blocking.

mechanisms.name: MCP tool-definition hash pinning
mechanisms.what: Snapshot every MCP server's advertised tool name, description and input schema into a committed lockfile with a SHA-256 per tool, and deny any call whose definition drifted.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Tool-definition approval does not survive server-side changes (CVSS 8.8). The two shipped stdio servers are inside gate-integrity's hashed surface, so the real exposure is consumer-added third-party servers — exactly where rug-pull risk lives.
mechanisms.evidence: Absence confirmed: no sha256/createHash/lock logic in pretool-mcp-guard.mjs; approved-tools.json records {server, version, readOnly, tools[]} and no hashes.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Extend pretool-mcp-guard.mjs with a hash comparison against a new tools/mcp-tools.lock.json; new scripts/check-mcp-lock.mjs; update docs/security/approved-tools.md, held in three-corner lockstep by docs-sync.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture mutates a tool description after locking -> the guard denies with a one-edit remedy; hook-contract asserts both the deny and the unchanged-definition allow.
mechanisms.risk: approved-tools.json is SEEDED precisely so a consumer's approval is not called tampering. The lockfile must inherit that classification or every consumer MCP approval reds gate-integrity. Re-read the 2026-07-28 MCP revision first — stateless core, Client ID Metadata Documents, RFC 9207 issuer validation — since it changes what a correct client must check.

mechanisms.name: Assisted-by trailer gate with no-agent-DCO
mechanisms.what: Require the exact trailer form at commit time and prohibit the agent adding Signed-off-by.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Post-hoc detection is not an option: a validated census across 180M+ repositories recovered only 3.3% of Claude Code commits by bot-account lookup. Only humans can legally certify the DCO.
mechanisms.evidence: Absence confirmed: zero matches for Assisted-by anywhere in the tree.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New git-commit rule in BASH_RULES in hooks/lib/guard-rules.mjs (the matcher already covers Bash|Monitor|PowerShell); new check-commit-attribution.mjs reading git log --format=%(trailers:only) as a PR-lane step.
mechanisms.proof: RULE_CANARIES deny/allow pair, closure enforced automatically by check-canary-coverage.mjs; gate fixture with a trailer-less commit -> exit 1; with an agent Signed-off-by -> exit 1.
mechanisms.risk: Human commits in the same branch must not red. Scope to commits whose author matches the agent identity, or require the trailer only when HARNESS_STOP_GATE was set. The model string must come from a launcher-set env var and, once telemetry lands, be cross-checked against the OTel model attribute — a self-declared model version is the one audit-relevant field the audit subject controls unilaterally.

mechanisms.name: Extend falsifiability closure to the compliance registers
mechanisms.harness: this repo's own check-canary-coverage.mjs, applied to a second domain
mechanisms.what: Every register row graded above the documentation floor must name a canary that injects the violation and observes the control fail; every canary claiming a register row must point at a live row.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A compliance claim with no demonstrable failing mode is vacuously true — the dominant failure mode of registers, and the exact thing this repo built the canary registry to prevent for gates. ASD's own tiers rank documentation and interviews POOR and testing with simulated activity EXCELLENT.
mechanisms.evidence: Structural; the closure machinery already exists and closes 44 steps, 27 lanes, 27 factory gates.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Add the registers as a second closure domain in scripts/check-canary-coverage.mjs; a registers key in tests/canary/injections.json; extend tests/gates/check-essential-eight.test.mjs.
mechanisms.proof: A register row with evidenceTier simulated-activity and no canary ref -> red; delete the row but leave the canary -> red.
mechanisms.risk: Some rows are genuinely documentation-tier and must be allowed no canary. The closure keys on the grade, so the grading vocabulary becomes load-bearing for a gate and needs its own drift check.

mechanisms.name: Compaction load-class lint
mechanisms.harness: Claude Code compaction table; this repo's CONTROL-PLANE-FACTS Fact 9
mechanisms.what: Assert that no invariant-marked line lives in a droppable load class, and that each SKILL.md keeps its load-bearing instructions in the first ~5,000 tokens. Deliberately NOT the re-injection hook.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Rules with paths: frontmatter and nested CLAUDE.md are documented as lost until a matching file is read again; skill bodies are re-injected but truncated at 5,000 tokens keeping the START. Fact 9 already concludes the doctrine is satisfied by construction, so the lint mechanises what two file headers currently hold alone.
mechanisms.evidence: Vendor documentation for the load classes; Fact 9 for the repo's own position.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New scripts/check-instruction-load-class.mjs over template/base/.claude/rules/*.md, AGENTS.md and skills/*/SKILL.md; factory Stop chain and factoryGates. Cite Fact 9 in its // SOURCE: header.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture moves a MUST-marked invariant into a paths:-scoped rule -> red; fixture pushes a skill's locked-order recipe past 5,000 tokens -> red.
mechanisms.risk: Token counting offline needs a byte heuristic (~3.5 B/token) to stay hermetic — CONTRIBUTING forbids a gate hitting a live endpoint.

mechanisms.name: Bounded gate output with spill-to-file logs
mechanisms.harness: Prime Agent OutputAccumulator; Claude Code's own Bash tool
mechanisms.what: Write full gate output to a log file and return a tail plus the path.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Gate output currently lands whole in the Stop feedback where only the last 4,000 chars survive — bloating the retry payload AND discarding the head. This is the recoverable half of Prime Agent's context-as-a-variable benefit, at S effort and with no substrate.
mechanisms.evidence: Prime Agent uses a bounded tail plus spill to a temp file, truncateHead for reads and truncateTail for command output; Claude Code's Bash tool does the same at ~30,000 chars.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: tools/lib/gate.mjs (failures/ok already own the output shape) writing to .harness/gate-logs/<run>/<gate>.log; stop-validate-gate.mjs emits tail plus path; gitignore the directory.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture gate emitting 200k lines -> the Stop block contains the tail and a resolvable path, and the log holds the full text. Today the head is unrecoverable.
mechanisms.risk: Log accumulation across a long run — trim by run id the way turn-outcomes already trims to KEEP=200.

mechanisms.name: invariants.json register + property closure
mechanisms.what: Declare the invariant surfaces — authz decisions, tenancy scoping, crypto envelope/AAD, keyset pagination, money and units — and close register <-> property both ways. Do NOT re-add fast-check; it is already pinned.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: fast-check ^4.9.0 already ships in the workspace catalog and fuzzyScore.test.ts already demonstrates the correct discipline — fixed seed, one public surface, an independent oracle. The missing half is the register, not the library.
mechanisms.evidence: Agents include tests in only 49.6% of code-changing PRs and miss error-handling constructs at 86.0% Java / 81.0% Python.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New template/base/tools/invariants.json (write-guard-protected, in ESCAPE_LISTS) plus check-invariants.mjs as a chain step.
mechanisms.proof: Register row with no matching property -> red; a property whose declared invariant is absent from the register -> red. The shipped scaffold is green on day one.
mechanisms.risk: Properties without an INDEPENDENT oracle are tautologies that re-run the implementation. The register must require the oracle to be named, or this becomes the agent-written-test blind spot it exists to fix.

mechanisms.name: isolation: worktree for the three write-capable author agents
mechanisms.what: Bound the blast radius of dal-author, migration-rls-author and test-author. The eight reviewers are already structurally read-only.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Worktree isolation enforces four checks including blocking git redirected via -C/--git-dir/GIT_DIR and blocking statically untraceable command shapes, with the shared .git carved out so commits still work.
mechanisms.evidence: All eight reviewers confirmed carrying disallowedTools: Write, Edit, machine-asserted by docs-sync via agent-roster.mjs and sha-locked in agents.lock.json.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: isolation: worktree on the three author agents; a .worktreeinclude carrying .env.local and .dev-auth/; extend docs-sync's roster assertion to require the field on any write-capable agent.
mechanisms.proof: Roster assertion reds when a write-capable agent omits isolation; the cc-floor check reds below 2.1.163.
mechanisms.risk: Hard-gated by Fact 10: two worktree sandbox escapes patched at 2.1.84 (CVE-2026-40068) and 2.1.163 (CVE-2026-55607). Also, -p runs never clean up their worktrees — teardown must be explicit.

mechanisms.name: SBOM completeness gate
mechanisms.what: Gate the emitted SBOM on actually declaring a graph — edges present, orphan share below a committed threshold, unresolvable components landing in an explicit unknown set rather than reading as clean.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: This is the repo's own 'absence is not a control' rule applied to the supply-chain surface.
mechanisms.evidence: Of 78,612 real-world SBOMs, 52.9% declare no dependency edges at all; median orphan share 93% among those with a dependency block and >=50 components; an explicit unknown level recovered recall 0.600 -> 0.950.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New tools/check-sbom-completeness.mjs reading the syft SPDX output template/modules/ci-provenance already produces; run between the SBOM step and the upload so an incomplete SBOM never becomes a signed artefact.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture SBOM with zero edges -> exit 1; 93% orphan share -> exit 1; the shipped scaffold's SBOM -> green.
mechanisms.risk: Threshold drift as the dependency tree grows — ratchet rather than fix.

mechanisms.name: Currency discipline for the floors
mechanisms.what: Give every row in tools/eol.json and tools/framework-floor.json a reviewedOn date and a calendar-kind obligation, so staleness reds in the scheduled hygiene lane and never on a PR. Extend to any pinned external version and to each dated fact in CONTROL-PLANE-FACTS.md.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: These are gates whose correctness decays on a wall clock with no code change — exactly the class the obligations register's calendar kind exists for. This research demonstrated the failure itself: it asserted a package version that the registry contradicts.
mechanisms.evidence: Self-demonstrated. See correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: reviewedOn fields in tools/eol.json and tools/framework-floor.json; rows in scripts/obligations.json (kind: calendar); assertions in check-obligations.mjs under --clockful only.
mechanisms.proof: A row whose reviewedOn precedes the staleness window reds under --clockful and stays green on the clockless PR run — the asymmetry is the test.
mechanisms.risk: None material; reuses machinery already unit-tested in tests/gates/obligations.test.mjs.

mechanisms.name: Stamped / diff-scoped Stop chain
mechanisms.harness: this repo's own stampGate machinery, applied to a surface it never covered
mechanisms.what: Extend stampGate to the pure-node Stop steps and route the two coverage-instrumented suites through a changed-package filter, forcing a full run when CI=true or the governor's fingerprint shows the tree moved outside the filtered set.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The committed measurement (24337 ms validate, 50531 ms stopWall) was taken against the seeded scaffold. The two coverage suites dominate turn latency and grow with the consumer's real suite, and the documented remedy today is a human commenting steps out of a write-protected config.
mechanisms.evidence: stampGate is applied to 12 validate gates and never to a Stop step.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: template/base/tools/lib/stamp-inputs.mjs extended to diff-coverage, duplication, i18n, test-quality, mobile-perf, reviewer-verdicts; unit and mobile-unit through a filter derived from tools/exports-walls.json.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture where only a doc changes -> stamped steps skip and the chain still reds on an injected violation in a declared stamp input, the closure tests/gates/hash-inputs.test.mjs already asserts for the validate side.
mechanisms.risk: A stamp whose input list is incomplete is a silently disabled gate. Every reviewed floor whose purpose is to re-judge unchanged code must be in the input list.

mechanisms.name: Factory-side private eval, and the first headless lane
mechanisms.what: Twenty tasks from this repo's own merged PRs — parent commit pinned, issue text as the prompt, merged diff and test delta hidden — run headless in a worktree, scored with the existing gate exit codes, persisting trajectory JSONL. Split into a replay-gated regression lane (pinned model, per-PR) and a live lane (model comparison, per-release). NEVER shipped in template/base.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Every claim in the repo today is about a CONTROL; none is about an OUTCOME. Scoring with gate exit codes means no LLM judge is needed for the primary metric — an advantage this repo already has and most evaluators do not.
mechanisms.evidence: SpecBench visible/held-out gaps to 100pp; scaffold alone moves SWE-bench Verified 10–20 points; replay misscores model-switching comparisons.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New tests/eval/ with tasks/*.json and run.mjs driving claude -p --output-format stream-json per worktree; a scheduled factory workflow.
mechanisms.proof: The eval is itself the proof instrument: a harness change may not regress the first-try-green rate below the committed baseline. Until it exists, the repo cannot distinguish 'produces world-class systems' from 'produces systems that satisfy this harness'.
mechanisms.risk: Cost ~$30–80 per 20-task sweep at Opus 5 rates, ~$200–500 for a 3-seed 2-arm A/B, plus non-determinism. This lane is the TRIGGER Fact 5 names: the moment it lands, the whole CI-agentic control batch stops being hypothetical and must be re-opened as one unit.

mechanisms.name: AI change-record attestation
mechanisms.harness: in-toto / SLSA / GitHub artifact attestations; SOC 2 CC8.1
mechanisms.what: One signed record per merged change binding prompt_id and session_id, the model id (from telemetry, not self-declaration), commit and tree digests, every gate verdict with the tree state it judged, reviewer verdicts, the human approver, and the CI run id.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: This is the artefact that converts world-class internal discipline into portable external evidence. Today every register is legible only to another in-house .mjs, and an auditor can neither check nor tamper-detect any of it.
mechanisms.evidence: actions/attest takes an arbitrary predicate-type with a 16MB predicate over OIDC — no keys, no Python.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New scripts/gen-change-record.mjs joining the Stop ledger with git trailers, the validate verdict JSON and the reviewer ledger; an actions/attest step reusing template/modules/ci-provenance; scripts/check-change-record.mjs gating on gh attestation verify --format=json.
mechanisms.proof: Gate reds when the verify JSON is absent, when predicate fields are incomplete, or when the recorded tree digest does not match HEAD.
mechanisms.risk: Three limits to write into the header rather than paper over. No registered in-toto predicate for AI authorship exists (RFC #554 open since 2026-05-19, no maintainer response), so the URI is self-minted and will churn. There is no agent-identity primitive, so the record is signed provenance about a partly self-declared actor. And Rekor is a PUBLIC transparency log while this repo ships an E2EE module — the record must carry hashes and identifiers, never prompt text.

mechanisms.name: CycloneDX Attestations export of the compliance registers
mechanisms.what: Serialize essential-eight.json and scripts/obligations.json into standards, requirements, claims, evidence, assessors and non-conformance.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The repo's existing reachability/outcome split and product/organisation boundary map onto CDXA's fields almost one-to-one, so this is a serializer over data already held.
mechanisms.evidence: Field names were NOT confirmed against the JSON schema in this session — only against the capability page.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New scripts/gen-cdxa.mjs emitting a .cdx.json beside the SPDX SBOM; attest it as a second subject in the change-record step.
mechanisms.proof: Round-trip test asserting every graded register row appears as exactly one claim, reusing the double-counting discipline essential-eight.json already states.
mechanisms.risk: Validate with a vendored schema, never a network fetch, or the gate stops being hermetic.

mechanisms.name: Gate determinism harness
mechanisms.what: Run every gate twice — once clean, once under a perturbed environment (TZ, LC_ALL, umask, HOME, CI and GITHUB_* presence, PATH order, cwd path length, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, shuffled readdir order) — and assert byte-identical verdicts and output hashes.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A gate that disagrees with itself is quarantined, not noted. This discharges the lane-environment-porosity lesson the repo has already paid for once.
mechanisms.evidence: The corpus initially claimed no literature exists here; that was wrong. Two 2026 papers address harness determinism directly and should be read first.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New scripts/check-gate-determinism.mjs spawning each gate twice with a mutated env; scheduled hygiene lane; emits determinism.json as an input to the change record.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture gate that reads process.env.TZ diverges across the matrix and is quarantined; the shipped gates are stable.
mechanisms.risk: Cost and flake noise. Treat a first divergence as a quarantine plus an obligations row rather than an immediate hard red.

mechanisms.name: @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime as an opt-in module
mechanisms.what: Whole-process wrapping so the seven hooks and two MCP servers sit inside the boundary they enforce. Opt-in module only, never the default.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The built-in Bash sandbox does not cover hooks, MCP servers or the file tools — which for this repo is the whole enforcement surface. srt is the only documented fix.
mechanisms.evidence: Beta Research Preview at 0.0.67; docker documented incompatible; unix sockets blocked; Linux needs bubblewrap + socat and on Ubuntu 24.04+ a root sysctl.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New template/modules/sandbox-runtime/ shipping .srt-settings.json plus a pnpm claude:sandboxed script that ALWAYS passes --settings; README stating the Supabase carve-out.
mechanisms.proof: Module gate asserts --settings is present and that denyWrite covers .claude/ — without it srt starts anyway with network blocked and writes confined to built-in paths, which looks like success. A silent-fallback start must be distinguishable from a loaded policy.
mechanisms.risk: Beta config format may change; pin exactly and add a ramp row. Never default it while it is beta. 'Rootless' holds honestly on macOS and only conditionally in Actions — that asymmetry must be written into gates-catalog.

mechanisms.name: Learned-lesson row kind in the obligations register
mechanisms.harness: AHE; qualified by Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit
mechanisms.what: A row kind carrying a prediction recorded at edit time and CHECKED at the next release, constrained to reference an existing capability id or a shipped .mjs check. A lesson that cannot be expressed as an executable check does not get a row.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The ramp/obligation machinery is already a stricter Continual Harness than Prime Agent's — rampNote throws when until <= minVersion, reds an unconsumed return value, reds a ramp below the lineage floor, and ratchets deadlines against the previous release tag. Prime Agent's ledger has no expiry, no reviewer verdict, and an expectedOutcome field nothing validates.
mechanisms.evidence: AHE Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 69.7% -> 77.0% with gains localised to tools/middleware/memory and NOT the system prompt. Counterweight: harness benefit is non-monotonic and strong-tier models benefit least.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New kind in scripts/obligations.json plus prediction/verified_at/outcome fields; judgements in scripts/lib/obligations.mjs; new scripts/check-refinement-predictions.mjs; a hygiene rule rejecting prose-only refinement diffs.
mechanisms.proof: A row whose prediction was falsified and neither reverted nor re-argued reds at the next release; a prose-only proposal reds.
mechanisms.risk: Explicitly sequenced AFTER the eval. Building the mechanism before the measurement is the exact error 2605.30621 warns about, and Prime Intellect's own Factorio case shows an unmeasured refinement loop optimises toward cheating.

mechanisms.name: Exhaustive authz decision-table enumeration
mechanisms.harness: lightweight formal methods, reduced to pure-Node enumeration
mechanisms.what: Declare role x tenant x row-ownership x operation x auth-assurance-level as data and execute the full cross-product against the real policy via the existing pgTAP runner.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: RLS is the one artefact in this stack whose state space is small enough to enumerate totally, and it is where a silent agent error is catastrophic and least visible. The in-flight MFA/AAL2 work makes the assurance-level dimension load-bearing now.
mechanisms.evidence: Structural. No TLA+, no Alloy, no JVM required.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New template/base/tools/authz-decision-table.json (write-guard-protected, sha-pinned, in ESCAPE_LISTS); enumeration inside the existing check-rls-manifest.mjs / check-tenancy.mjs pgTAP path.
mechanisms.proof: Any cell the table does not declare, or whose observed verdict disagrees with the declaration, reds — and the coverage matrix is emitted so an assessor sees totality rather than taking it on trust.
mechanisms.risk: Honest limit for the header: it proves the DECLARED dimensions are total, not that the dimensions are the right ones. That half stays with the reviewer, and saying so is what keeps the gate from being a vacuous completeness claim.

mechanisms.name: Structural-rot ratchet
mechanisms.what: Measure erosion (complexity mass in functions above CC 10) and verbosity (flagged plus clone lines over LOC) and ratchet the slope per release.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Long-horizon failure is monotone accumulation, not a single wrong step, and prompts demonstrably cannot fix it — an anti-slop prompt cut initial verbosity 34.5% while leaving the degradation SLOPE unchanged.
mechanisms.evidence: Erosion rose in 80% of trajectories, mean high-complexity function count 4.1 -> 37.0; verbosity worsened in 89.8%; agent code 2.2x more verbose than 48 maintained human repos which stayed flat; cost grew 2.9x with no correctness gain.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New template/base/tools/check-structural-rot.mjs using the TypeScript compiler API or ts-morph plus a token-shingle clone detector; ratchet in tools/validate.floor.json.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture tree with an injected 40-branch function exceeds the erosion ratchet and reds; the shipped scaffold is green and its values become the baseline.
mechanisms.risk: Adds a parser dependency to a zero-runtime-dep repo — scope to devDependencies and pin in the framework floor.

mechanisms.name: Org-side spend ceiling as an autonomous-run precondition
mechanisms.harness: Anthropic Usage/Cost and Spend Limits APIs
mechanisms.what: Make an org-side spend limit a documented launch precondition, and gate on the DECLARATION rather than the API.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The run governor is self-reported by the run it governs — a diagnostic that authorizes nothing, which is the correct classification and also the reason it is not a ceiling. An org-side limit is the one control an autonomous run cannot spend past.
mechanisms.evidence: Shipped to Claude Enterprise July 2026 with ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY and history from 1 Jan 2026. Per-workspace or per-key scoping is UNCONFIRMED, and whether subscription runs are covered at all is UNKNOWN.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: New template/base/docs/harness/autonomous-run.md launch contract; check-autonomous-preconditions.mjs asserting the governor's ceiling references a named org-side cap.
mechanisms.proof: Fixture launch contract with no ceiling reference -> exit 1.
mechanisms.risk: Requires Enterprise plus an admin key, so it is an operator precondition rather than something a generated project can enforce. The gate must check the DECLARATION and say so, or it claims enforcement it cannot perform.

mechanisms.name: Plugin + marketplace delivery evaluation
mechanisms.harness: Claude Code plugins and enterprise-managed marketplaces
mechanisms.what: A written comparison of plugin delivery against the current bespoke fleet-delivery path, and adoption only if it wins.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The hardest problem this factory has is fleet delivery — fourteen touchpoints per gate, a configSteps injection path anchored on single-line entries, a seeded-vs-owned taxonomy, all bespoke. A versioned plugin plus an enterprise-managed marketplace allowlist is the vendor's answer to that exact problem, and it supplies the managed-policy floor docs/security/managed-settings.md documents but does not ship.
mechanisms.evidence: Plugins ship hooks as hooks/hooks.json at the plugin root in settings.json format. Enterprise-managed plugins appear at managed scope users cannot modify.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: A comparison in template/base/docs/harness/; if adopted, hooks/hooks.json in .claude-plugin/ and an extension of scripts/check-plugin-manifest.mjs.
mechanisms.proof: check-plugin-manifest.mjs reds a plugin-declared hook not also wired in settings.json, so a plugin-delivered enforcement layer cannot silently replace the file-delivered one.
mechanisms.risk: Plugin subagents silently ignore hooks, mcpServers and permissionMode — a naive migration of the reviewer roster into a plugin would drop exactly the per-agent controls next12 adds. Deciding not to use plugins is defensible; never evaluating them is the gap.

mechanisms.name: Bounded review-revise loop
mechanisms.what: On a red turn, feed the structured diagnosis back into a revision of the SAME patch rather than sampling alternatives; cap at four rounds; stop at first clean.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Serial compute on the trajectory that already has context beats parallel compute on candidates that then need a discriminator, because discrimination is the broken part.
mechanisms.evidence: Review-guided iterative revision reached 38.4% from a 22.9% baseline within 4 rounds at 2.44 samples average, beating verifier-based best-of-16 (25.6%) at equal budget. CodeMonkeys bounds the prize: random selection 45.8%, achieved 57.4%, oracle 69.8%.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: A slash command or skill driving the loop, with a round counter in .harness/loop-state.json that stop-validate-gate.mjs reads; convergence via a stable digest over the sorted findings set (reuse pathStateDigest — findings are discrete, no embeddings needed).
mechanisms.proof: Fixture where two consecutive rounds produce an identical findings digest terminates on the K=2 patience rule; a fixture exhausting four rounds reds with a distinct reason.
mechanisms.risk: Ceiling effect — the measured lift on the strongest generator was ~3pp versus ~29pp on the weakest. On Opus 5 this may be mostly tax. Sequence after the eval.

mechanisms.name: Kernel sandbox underneath the command guard
mechanisms.what: Both vendors replaced 'inspect the command string and decide' with OS-level confinement. The text guard becomes advisory; the kernel is the control.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A pattern-matching guard can only deny commands it can parse, and an agent reaches the same effect by another route — shell indirection, a heredoc, a language runtime, an npm lifecycle hook.
mechanisms.evidence: Primary vendor docs for both. No published head-to-head on sandbox vs pattern-guard escape rates — the mechanism is verified, the efficacy claim is architectural rather than measured.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Subsumed by now3.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.

mechanisms.name: Three-tier autonomy: allowlist, sandbox, adjudicator
mechanisms.what: Allowlisted calls run immediately; other shell commands run in the sandbox when possible; everything else goes to a classifier subagent returning allow, take-a-different-approach, or ask-human. Neither vendor asks the human first.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: In headless runs there is nobody to approve, so a binary allowlist forces a choice between stalling and disabling the guard. The take-a-different-approach verdict is a repair channel rather than a veto.
mechanisms.evidence: Primary docs both. No published false-allow / false-deny rates from either vendor — which is why this is recorded and not proposed.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Not proposed. Adding an unmeasured LLM to the enforcement path needs a legit-but-unlisted command corpus first, which does not exist here.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.

mechanisms.name: Clean-context reviewer denied the coder's trajectory
mechanisms.what: A review agent reads the PR with no shared context from the coding agent, deliberately not handed the coder's trajectory.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: A reviewer that inherits the author's transcript inherits its rationalisations and blind spots — it confirms rather than tests.
mechanisms.evidence: Vendor self-report: 2 bugs per PR, 58% severe, no baseline, no false-positive rate, no external replication. Directionally corroborated by Amp's independent Oracle design.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Reviewer subagents here already start with fresh contexts. The unexamined half is the INPUT contract — whether they receive the main transcript and the author's justification. Worth checking; not proposed as a roadmap item because it was not verified against this repo in-session.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.

mechanisms.name: Fan out reads, serialize writes
mechanisms.what: Multiple agents contribute intelligence while writes stay single-threaded. The multi-agent shapes that work are read-only subagents and map-reduce with one writer.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Two concurrent writers each make hundreds of unstated choices, and no merge step can reconcile them because the conflicting decisions are not in the diff.
mechanisms.evidence: Two Cognition essays a year apart holding the same invariant. Directional — no benchmark isolates parallel-write cost.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Already held: all eight reviewers are structurally read-only and machine-asserted. next12 extends the containment to the three authors.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.

mechanisms.name: Trigger-scoped knowledge instead of always-on context
mechanisms.what: Pair a trigger description with the content and retrieve when relevant, rather than loading everything on every turn.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Measured rather than argued: context files raised inference cost ~19–20% while LLM-generated ones cut success ~3% and developer-written ones gained only ~4%. Agents anchor hard on whatever the file mentions.
mechanisms.evidence: 138 tasks, four agents, both file provenances. Countervailing companion paper: 28.64% median runtime reduction and 16.58% output-token reduction with comparable completion — cheaper, not more correct.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: NOT proposed as a roadmap item, and the reason matters: this repo's always-on rules are deliberately advisory with the gates as the invariant, so the studied failure mode — the file being the only thing holding the rule — does not apply in the same way. The measurable question is cost, which needs telemetry (next1) before it can be answered here.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.
mechanisms.risk: This is the mechanism most likely to be wrongly imported. The studies measure context files as a CORRECTNESS mechanism; here they are a probability-raiser behind a deterministic floor. Do not delete doctrine on the strength of a study that measured a different thing.

mechanisms.name: Pre-apply parse gate: apply, parse, revert, return the error
mechanisms.what: The edit command applies the change, runs a restricted linter, and if new errors appear the edit is REVERTED and the agent receives the error plus its proposed change and the original code.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Syntactically broken code never enters the file or the transcript, so it cannot be reasoned over, copied, or discovered ten turns later.
mechanisms.evidence: Controlled ablation on SWE-bench Lite: full 18.0%, no linting 15.0%. This is one of the few mechanisms in the whole corpus with a real on/off number.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: pretool-write-guard.mjs already matches Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit and could reconstruct post-edit content in memory and parse it. Not in the roadmap because it adds a parser dependency and the synthesis ranked other items above it — but it is the strongest-evidenced unadopted mechanism in the corpus and deserves a decision rather than silence.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.

mechanisms.name: Environment normalization as an autonomy control
mechanisms.what: Set PAGER/MANPAGER/LESS/TQDM_DISABLE etc. on every command and truncate oversized observations head-and-tail with an elided count.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: The two things that actually end unattended runs are a command blocking on a pager and one command's output eating the context window. Both are configuration, not carefulness, and both are invisible until they happen.
mechanisms.evidence: Config values read from the project's YAML docs.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: One env block in template/base/.claude/settings.json, asserted by check-wiring.mjs so it cannot drift. This is the same lesson as the lane-environment-porosity memory, applied to the agent instead of the lane — cheap, and not in the roadmap only because the synthesis capped `now` at six.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.

mechanisms.name: Event-sourced run ledger with deterministic risk labels
mechanisms.what: One chronological append-only event log every component reads from and appends to, so the agent is a pure step(state)->action and every run replays by construction.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: An append-only log makes an unattended run auditable and reproducible after the fact, and a risk label gives policy somewhere to attach that is not the prompt.
mechanisms.evidence: Architecture verified in two papers. The Condenser's 'up to 2x cost reduction with no degradation' is self-reported, not replicated.
mechanisms.repoIntegrationPoint: Partly present: .harness/reviewer-ledger.jsonl and turn-outcomes.jsonl. later2's change record is the generalisation, and it is scoped to the audit artefact rather than to replacing the hook architecture. Note also the docker-socket coupling OpenHands itself reversed — an anti-pattern to avoid.
mechanisms.proof: n/a — recorded for understanding.

rejected.name: Prime Agent's RLM execution substrate (one tool, persistent TS REPL, context-as-a-variable)
rejected.why: Structurally impossible and probably negative-value. Prime Agent's core move is allToolNames = new Set(['ipython']); there is no configuration seam in the Claude Code CLI that lets a harness collapse the tool menu. Every enforcement layer here is keyed to built-in tool names — PreToolUse matchers are exact tool names, the write-guard's ~90 protected path regexes operate on Edit/Write/MultiEdit payloads, the mcp-guard parses mcp__server__tool. A ts_exec substrate would sit BESIDE all of that, not under it, and the rule table would see one opaque call whose contents it cannot inspect. On value: Anthropic's own counter-result is that sequential single-call workflows — which is exactly 'run gate, read verdict, fix, re-run' — showed unchanged scores at ~8% HIGHER cost. Node also documents that stripTypeScriptTypes output is not stable across versions, which collides with the determinism rule for gates.

rejected.name: Typed capability broker (tools/broker.mjs with a Zod verb registry)
rejected.why: Downstream of a substrate that is not being built, and self-defeating even if it were. With no code-execution action space there is nothing to broker: PreToolUse already IS the chokepoint over a pure-data 134-rule table with symlink resolution and default-deny MCP. Worse, the research conceded the fatal problem in its own open questions — two independent enforcement lists that must agree is a defect generator — which is precisely the lesson scripts/check-escape-registry.mjs exists to encode. Adding a third list to reconcile is a regression dressed as an upgrade.

rejected.name: isolated-vm, node:vm, Node --permission, or Deno as a containment boundary
rejected.why: Each either reintroduces a banned toolchain or is a documented non-boundary. isolated-vm needs node-gyp, whose stated prerequisite is a supported version of Python — it fails the no-Python constraint outright, and its README says maintenance mode. Node states flatly that node:vm is not a security mechanism and calls --permission a seat belt malicious code can bypass. Deno's docs call --allow-run=deno especially dangerous because the child can re-invoke with --allow-all. docs/harness/README.md already says 'Guards are tripwires, not sandboxes' — an honest caveat is strictly better than a fake boundary.

rejected.name: Semgrep or Rego/OPA as the policy-as-code engine
rejected.why: Semgrep distributes via pip, brew or Docker; its npm package is version 0.0.1, last published roughly six years ago — adopting it silently reintroduces Python or Docker. Rego does evaluate rootless via opa-wasm, but the .wasm must be produced by the Go `opa build -t wasm` at authoring time, and Rego cannot see a TypeScript AST — only JSON someone already extracted. The extraction step is where essentially all the logic in the 64 check-*.mjs scripts (44 shipped, 20 factory) lives, so this buys auditor-legible policy text at the price of a second language plus a Go toolchain while leaving the hard part untouched.

rejected.name: A consumer-shipped held-out test suite
rejected.why: Strongest evidence in the corpus, impossible delivery. The agent runs inside the generated project, so anything shipped to template/base/tools/heldout/** is a readable file in the consumer's own tree by construction, and a read-deny hook is a text tripwire over paths the agent can enumerate. Both named workarounds — CI-fetched or encrypted-at-rest — break the CONTRIBUTING rule that a gate must be hermetic, and both fail for an offline fork. The factory-side variant survives as later1.

rejected.name: Aider-style PageRank repo map over a tree-sitter def/ref graph
rejected.why: L effort, adds web-tree-sitter WASM grammars and graphology to a repo whose stated design is plain Node ESM with zero runtime dependencies, and the value is unmeasured against the current regime. Every published repo-map result predates frontier agentic search and 1M context. Building an L-effort dependency-adding mechanism against unmeasured value fails the repo's own gate-proposal bar.

rejected.name: The CI-agentic control batch (PermissionDenied ledger, dontAsk, Setup hook, system/init gating, ultracode flag, Rule-of-Two analyzer)
rejected.why: Rejected as a batch on a precondition, not on merit. CONTROL-PLANE-FACTS Fact 5 records the search for `claude -p`, `claude --print` and `anthropics/claude-code` across both workflow trees and finds no matches: no CI lane in this repository spawns Claude at all. Fact 5 even anticipates the exact risk — that in non-interactive mode a tool call is denied when no PermissionRequest hook decides — and concludes the risk is not live today. Re-open all six as ONE UNIT the moment later1 lands; that lane is the trigger.

rejected.name: PreToolUse re-injection of path-scoped rules after compaction
rejected.why: Fact 9 already carries the full survival table and concludes the doctrine is satisfied by construction, because boundaries.md and mobile-server-split.md both open by declaring themselves best-effort with the gates as the invariant. Re-injection would spend a hook budget defending prose the repo has deliberately decided is not load-bearing. Fact 9 also pre-emptively rejects the alternative — watching InstructionsLoaded with load_reason 'compact' — as resting on undocumented behaviour. Only the load-class LINT survives, as next9.

rejected.name: A cold-start refuter agent / forced-refutation promotion stage
rejected.why: Feasible but premature and probably the wrong direction. The source study ships no non-adversarial baseline arm, so its 79–83% kill rate is not evidence the survivors beat a plain 'quote your evidence verbatim' bar — which is cheaper and is next2. Meanwhile the panel-economics result argues the existing eleven-agent roster is already over-built. Adding a twelfth agent before measuring the existing eleven is spending into an unmeasured asymptote. Measure n_eff first; deleting reviewers is a legitimate outcome.

rejected.name: Whole-session sandbox-runtime wrap as the DEFAULT posture
rejected.why: Rejected as a default only; survives as later5. Docker is documented incompatible and unix sockets are blocked, while the Stop chain's rls-isolation step runs against local Supabase — excluding it reopens exactly the surface being sandboxed. Compounding that, srt is a Beta Research Preview whose configuration format may change, and shipping a beta config schema into every generated project collides with release-lockstep and version-pinning discipline.

rejected.name: Flipping harden-runner to egress-policy: block
rejected.why: Already a written decision, not an oversight. harden-runner is SHA-pinned across all 13 workflows and the audit-mode rationale is recorded in template/base/github/zizmor.yml — block mode is Linux-only on GitHub-hosted runners, so setting it on a macOS or Windows job and reporting it as enforced is exactly the vacuous green the conformance doctrine forbids. An allowed-endpoints list also drifts with dependencies, reproducing the nondeterministic-CI-policy failure already recorded for minimumReleaseAge.

rejected.name: Re-implementing controls this repo already ships
rejected.why: Four proposals described machinery that already exists in a better form. Property-based testing: fast-check ^4.9.0 is pinned in the catalog and fuzzyScore.test.ts already runs with a fixed seed against an independent subsequence oracle — only the register is new (next11). Mutation testing: check-mutation-ratchet.mjs already compares the exact SET of surviving mutants against a write-protected baseline and its header explicitly rejects the score threshold the research also warns against. Attestation plumbing: template/modules/ci-provenance already runs actions/attest-build-provenance plus an SPDX SBOM and verifies with gh attestation verify IN CI, with the honest limit written down. Reviewer read-only enforcement: all eight reviewers already carry disallowedTools: Write, Edit, machine-asserted and sha-locked — which is TeamBench's 3.6x enforcement win, already banked.

rejected.name: Building cron scheduling, push-notification escalation, or cloud microVM sessions
rejected.why: Claude Code already ships all three: CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete, PushNotification since v2.1.110, Remote Control for terminal-less runs, and claude --cloud full-microVM sessions. The research proposed porting Prime Agent's `prime-agent schedule` and listed 'no human handoff/notification' as an unfilled rung — both are stale-memory artefacts. Use the native tools.

rejected.name: Expanding tests/canary/injections.json into a prompt-injection corpus
rejected.why: Rejected as framed, replaced by next5. injections.json is a falsifiability registry with keys steps(44), hookRules(3), lanes(27), factoryGates(27), factoryLanes(22) — excellent at proving each gate CAN go red once. Conflating it with a security eval would corrupt both, and the adaptive-attack literature is unambiguous that a static payload measures string equality rather than resistance.

rejected.name: TDD enforcement inside the agent loop
rejected.why: Measured not to work. A blind evaluation found no discernible quality difference, with non-TDD solutions ranking first and second; TDD consumed 2.96x–8.5x more tokens and produced SHALLOWER suites; mutation scores indistinguishable; agents routinely faked the red step and wrote tautological tests. The productive versions of this instinct are mutation testing (already shipped) and no-op ablation (reachable via next11).

rejected.name: Anthropic API context editing and the memory tool
rejected.why: No seam in the runtime this repo targets. clear_tool_uses_20250919, memory_20250818 and compact_20260112 are Claude Developer Platform features with beta headers, and the harness configures the Claude Code CLI rather than calling the API directly. The reported effect sizes are the largest in the corpus and worth revisiting IF Claude Code exposes them, but adopting them today would be the same category error as the RLM substrate: designing against the Agent SDK while shipping for the CLI.

correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.subject: Prime Agent's implementation language
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStatedInTheRequest: Prime Agent is written in Python.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.correction: It is TypeScript. GitHub language bytes: TypeScript 11,773,264 vs Python 167,606; repo.language == TypeScript. The Python is one component — prime-agent-runtime, an IPython kernel the TypeScript host drives as the model's action substrate. The confusion is understandable: every writeup leads with 'the model writes and runs Python in a persistent IPython kernel'.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.consequence: The requested TypeScript port is already done upstream. The residual question is whether to replace the IPython substrate with a Node one, answered NO.

correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.subject: Prime Agent's root-privilege requirement
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStatedInTheRequest: Prime Agent has a root privilege issue to eliminate.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.correction: No hard root requirement exists. The project's docs state three separate times that the worker/kernel split is not a security sandbox and run with the client's OS permissions. The only sudo is install.sh bootstrapping Node via apt/apk, gated on Node being absent and skipped entirely on a machine that has it (Homebrew on macOS). The real-world complaint is likely issue #705 — `npm install -g` failing with EACCES against a root-owned /usr/local prefix, fix PR #706 still unmerged. The one place root buys a capability is the OPTIONAL sandbox extension, and on macOS that is sandbox-exec, which needs no root at all.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.consequence: There is nothing to eliminate. The transferable lesson is narrower and still real: never npm install -g into a root-owned prefix.

correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.subject: Prime Agent's headline benchmark claims
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStatedBy: an earlier agent in this session, relaying the vendor
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStated: Reported results include ARC-AGI-3 at 95.5% on Opus 5 and from-scratch emulators on EmulatorBench.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.correction: The identification agent relayed the vendor's framing; the evidence deep-dive contradicted it. The 95.5% is vendor-run on the PUBLIC set; ARC Prize's verified semi-private row for Opus 5 is 30.2%, and ARC Prize policy requires public/semi-private agreement within ±15pp before a score is accepted — so the numbers are not comparable and Prime Agent appears on no verified leaderboard. EmulatorBench is Prime Intellect's own preview benchmark; the actual table is 0.208 / 0.275 / 0.047, and on Opus 5 CLAUDE CODE BEAT PRIME AGENT (0.062 vs 0.047). Across nine long-context benchmarks Prime Agent beats Claude Code on Opus 5 by ~1–2pp six times and loses three times. No SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench or SWE-Lancer entries exist.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.consequence: This is the single most decision-relevant correction in the artefact. For a repo already running Opus 5 in Claude Code, Prime Agent's harness gains are approximately zero — the large gains in its own tables are all on the weak open-weight model. It removes any argument for adopting its architecture wholesale.

correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.subject: @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime version
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStated: v0.0.71, asserted in two separate research legs.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.correction: The npm registry shows 0.0.67. Pin from a registry read, never from prose.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.consequence: Motivates next14 — currency discipline. This artefact demonstrated the exact failure mode that item exists to catch.

correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.subject: Claude Code hook event count
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStated: Given as 31 by one agent and 30 by another.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.correction: Not adjudicated. The direction is certain — materially more than the 4 events this repo binds (7 hook entries) — the exact count is not. Recorded as confidence low rather than picked.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.consequence: Any roadmap item depending on a specific new hook event must verify that event's existence and payload against current docs before implementation.

correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.subject: Gate-determinism literature
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStated: 'No published benchmark exists for gate-level determinism specifically', used to grade a mechanism medium.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.correction: False. Two 2026 papers address harness determinism directly (arXiv 2604.17025 CAAF; arXiv 2605.22166). Neither was opened in this session, so they are recorded as leads rather than as evidence.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.consequence: An unfalsifiable absence claim is exactly the class this repo's doctrine forbids. later4 must read both before proceeding.

correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.subject: The SBOM mechanism's own repoIntegrationPoint, corrected while implementing it in v0.10.0
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStatedBy: this artefact, mechanisms[].repoIntegrationPoint for the SBOM item
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.asStated: Add tools/check-sbom-completeness.mjs reading the syft SPDX output template/modules/ci-provenance already produces; run it between the SBOM step and the upload 'so an incomplete SBOM never becomes a signed artefact'.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.correction: Both halves are wrong, and the quoted clause is the load-bearing one. ORDERING: in template/modules/ci-provenance/github/workflows/provenance.yml the `Attest build provenance` step runs BEFORE the SBOM step, and its subject-path is `dist-pack/*.tgz` — the tarballs only. The SBOM is the subject of no attestation, so no gate placed anywhere in that job can stop an incomplete SBOM 'becoming a signed artefact': it was never going to be signed. A completeness gate there would still be worth having, but its claim is only that the UPLOADED artefact is complete, which is smaller and must not be stated as the other. PLACEMENT: ci-provenance is an opt-in MODULE and is triple-exempt from every canary closure this repo has — check-canary-coverage.mjs scopes `lanes` to template/base/github/workflows, `factoryLanes` to .github/workflows, and `factoryGates` to scripts/ — so a gate added there would have been the only new control in the release that nothing required a red-proof for.
correctionsAppliedToSourceResearch.consequence: v0.10.0 built it in the BASE tree instead: job `sbom-inventory` in template/base/github/workflows/osv-scan.yml, over `pnpm sbom` (CycloneDX, --lockfile-only) rather than syft SPDX, with tools/check-sbom.mjs closing the component set against pnpm-lock.yaml in both directions and tests/gates/sbom.test.mjs registered as the lane red-proof the base-tree closure demands. The module lane is unchanged. The honest claim is 'the daily inventory is provably complete', never 'an incomplete SBOM cannot be signed'.

reviewNotes: Two of the three premises in the originating request were false. That is recorded in corrections rather than smoothed away, because the research's value came substantially from discovering it.

The corpus contradicted itself once in a decision-relevant way (corr-3) and twice in minor ways (corr-4, corr-5). One agent's confident relay was corrected by another agent's primary-source check. No adjudication mechanism existed; the contradiction was caught by reading both. A future run should cross-check headline benchmark claims by construction.

Roughly a third of the mechanisms proposed by the survey agents were already implemented here, already deliberately decided against with written reasoning, or already adjudicated in design/CONTROL-PLANE-FACTS.md. The feasibility skeptic caught these; without a repo-aware critique stage the roadmap would have recommended re-building existing controls.

Evidence quality is highly uneven. The strongest items carry controlled ablations (SWE-agent linting 18.0% -> 15.0%). The weakest are vendor self-reports with no baseline (Devin Review's 2 bugs/PR). Tier placement in this artefact weighs evidence strength, not just claimed effect size.

The `now` tier is deliberately six items and deliberately small-effort-weighted. Four of six are S. This is a bias toward closing open paths over building new capability, which matches the gap analyst's finding that the repo needs anchoring rather than more controls.

This session did NOT open the arXiv papers. Every paper-derived figure carries relayed: true. Anyone acting on an effect size should read the paper first — several are load-bearing for tier placement.
